exceptions.evidence: Gifts to clients and prospects are capped at $50 per recipient per occasion. An occasion is one receipt; lines on it that name the same recipient are added together for the cap, and the $10 test applies to each line. Spend above the cap is a medium exception. Any gift of $10 or more must also name its recipient, in the line description or elsewhere on the expense; an unnamed gift at that value is a medium exception. Cards and small tokens under $10 need no named recipient. Gift cards and other cash equivalents fall under GIFT-02 alone and are not also tested here. Unnamed gifts are each tested on their own, and when both parts of GIFT-01 apply, one exception cites every line involved.
exceptions.explanation: GIFT-01 (Client gift cap) raises a medium exception on 'Sterling silver bracelet - client gift for A. Moreau, Halcyon Partners' ($180.00): per recipient $180.0 vs $50 cap; unnamed at $10+: none.

exceptions.evidence: Two or more receipts by the same employee, at the same merchant (by merchant name), on the same calendar date, are treated as a deliberate split when each one is at or below one of these thresholds but together they are above it: the $75 itemization threshold, when every receipt in the group is non-itemized (DOC-01); the employee's meal cap, compared per person (MEAL-01, REG-02, REG-03); or the $50 gift cap for one recipient (GIFT-01). This is an exception, at high severity, and applies to every receipt in the group. It replaces the threshold rule being split around: report the split, not a separate breach of that threshold.
exceptions.explanation: TIME-03 (Split transactions) raises a high exception on the receipt from Copper Skillet ($74.00 total): split transaction: meal spend per person vs the day's meal cap (MEAL-01, REG-02, REG-03): $74.00 (RCP-020) + $71.50 (RCP-021) = $145.50 > $75.00, each at or below it.
